content.text:
Silhouette: Four-legged gray wolf frame. Host frame: the gray wolf sets the outline, body size and overall frame. A single creature that combines a crab and a gray wolf. Head of the gray wolf, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. Details: gray wolf body and legs, with its own dense fur everywhere else, plain coat, no stripes or spots; from the crab, as parts and materials on the gray wolf's own body: claws grown from the front feet: each front foot ends in a pincer, held folded against the foot when the animal walks: heavy, knobbed, hard-shelled claws with a fixed and a moving finger; large evenly sized claws with black tips. Coat texture and patches follow the body outline. Declared fiction: arthropod parts at large size, shown with thick supporting legs. Bilaterally symmetrical, recognizable limbs, visible sense organs. Habitat cue (rocky coast): dark back and light belly (strong countershading). Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.

summary.text:
**Designing wolf-crab hybrid**
I'm planning the image around a gray wolf silhouette with crab claws replacing the front paws, keeping the wolf head, dense fur, and plain coat while folding the heavy pincers close to the feet.
**Refining hybrid anatomy details**
I'm working on a natural history illustration of a gray wolf with crab pincers for front feet, countershading, thick supporting legs, and a plain light background in side three-quarter view.
**Refining paw and leg anatomy**
I'm adjusting the front paws so the claws fold naturally against the foot and keeping them as feet only, while also making sure the hind legs read as wolf for the next generation.
